messages:
sanjay: FYI started the CUDA 11->12 roll for dedicated pools in us-west-2 about 30m ago. after the container rebuilds some inference pods are OOM/crashing on model init. logs show symbol errors and some NCCL hangs.

lina: ugh. any specific error lines?

sanjay: pasted a snippet from one crash:
```
ImportError: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so.12: undefined symbol: cuInit
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  failed to initialize cuBLAS handle
```

ajay: that usually points to a driver/runtime mismatch. which nvidia driver is on those nodes? CUDA 12 needs >= 525 driver iirc.

ops-bot: deploy: cuda-toolkit-upgrade started by sanjay (canary: us-west-2-c).

lina: checked node images — some hosts are on driver 520 (older kernel package), others on 535. we missed the nodepool upgrade in us-west-2-b.

maya: also seeing repeated NCCL timeouts when multi-gpu jobs start: messages like `NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed errno 14` then hangs for 30s and restart. network driver/kernel mismatch might be involved.

ajay: kernel mismatch + older OFED stacks cause ibverbs to break. that explains NCCL warnings. can we pin canary to single-gpu nodes while we reconcile drivers?

sanjay: yes. i've paused the rollout for other regions. rolling back the canary to CUDA 11 images now. however many images were auto-rebuilt with system gcc12 / glibc tweaks — some users compiled custom wheels that now fail at import time (C++ ABI issues).

lina: for short term: 1) drain multi-gpu pools in us-west-2-b, 2) mark nodes with driver <525 as ineligible for CUDA12, 3) rebuild a compatibility image using the old toolchain and set it as fallback.

ajay: ++ on fallback. also recommend adding a runtime check in the container entrypoint that validates driver vs cuda versions before loading heavy libs, e.g.:
```bash
CUDA_DRV_MAJOR=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader | cut -d. -f1)
if [ "$CUDA_DRV_MAJOR" -lt 525 ]; then
  echo "Driver too old for CUDA12; using fallback"
  exec /usr/local/bin/start-fallback
fi
```

maya: cost note — we had to move several workloads to smaller single-gpu nodes during the pause which increased queued time and caused a ~12% uplift in hourly burn for the cluster. finance asked for an incident note.

sanjay: filing a short blameless summary after we stabilize. action items: (sanjay) rollback canary images + pause rollout, (lina) tag nodepools and schedule driver upgrade to 535 across the fleet, (ajay) publish fallback images with older ABI and entrypoint checks, (maya) capture cost delta and notify finance.

lina: I'll also add a preflight verify job in the image CI that runs `nvidia-smi`, `ldd` checks for libcuda/libcublas, and a tiny NCCL ring test in a k8s job before we flip the flag.

ajay: and add a `--force-cuda-version` flag to internal deployer so image rebuilds don't silently pick the new base unless explicitly requested.

ops-bot: incident: cuda12-rollout-compat created (sev:low) by sanjay.

sanjay: thanks all. will update incident doc with timelines and follow-ups.
